rationale: AppContainer SID isolation, a private fixture store and explicit restricted authorization provide a suitable construction model. Keep host-issued HTTP probes under candidate credentials distinct from candidate-process OS probes; this does not demonstrate HTTP execution inside the child.

execution_conditions.condition: The trusted host must first verify that each actual fixture file and marker exists and is readable, then record candidate SID/PID and OS denial. Private store, authority DB and credentials must never enter candidate input/output staging.

The actual composed execution must prove that the candidate receives only one necessary input at a time and no intermediate per-item feedback. Existing engine unit tests are corroboration only; if this cannot be composed without new production interfaces, retain the C22-02 evidence gap.

Restart a new control-plane process against the same temporary DB/store, repeat API authorization and a new AppContainer file probe, and verify revoked credentials or missing isolation fail closed with qualification BLOCKED/ADVISORY.

limitations: Read-only design assessment; no construction or execution is performed in this review.
Does not authorize ordinary LIVE execution or BOUNDED_AUTO and does not relax CanaryStore LIVE restrictions.
Actual C22 construction and independent evidence review must be assigned separately.
